newsitem.title: USA: New Asian economic group to meet March 4.
newsitem.headline: New Asian economic group to meet March 4.

text.p: A new Asian economic group formed at the urging of the United States will hold its first meeting on March 4 in Tokyo to discuss economic and financial market issues, the U.S. Treasury said on Monday.

The G-6 meeting, which groups Japan, China, Singapore, Australia, Hong Kong and the United States, will be attended by finance ministry and central bank officials. It comes at a time when the United States is increasingly seeking to strengthen relations with its Asian trading partners, including China, a growing global economic powerhouse.

The United States will be represented by Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers, who will also meet on March 3 with his counterparts in Hong Kong, before travelling to Tokyo. The Tokyo meeting will also be attended by Federal Reserve officials including Fed governor Lawrence Meyer.
The officials will "discuss economic policy and financial market issues of mutual interest," the Treasury said in a statement.

Financial sources in Tokyo said the officials would examine macroeconomic policies, financial market supervision and foreign exchange rates. They will also explore possible responses in the event of an Asian version of Mexico's financial crisis, which required a fast-moving international rescue effort, the sources said.
